LESSON: READING 10.4.1 CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the relevance of oral narratives in modern society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify characters in monster narratives, (
2. explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (
3. appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 10.4.1 CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 10.4.1 CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify characters in monster narratives, (

What this means
In this part you learn to identify characters in monster narratives, (. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify characters in monster narratives, (.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify characters in monster narratives, (. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (

What this means
In this part you learn to explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify characters in monster narratives, ()

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits to a partner. (skill: explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, ()

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify characters in monster narratives, (.
3. Practise this skill: explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the relevance of oral narratives in modern society?
2. What should one consider when collecting narratives among people of varied socio-cultural backgrounds?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify characters in monster narratives, (.
5. Be able to: explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
